title: Zoom in: one message write at LOCAL_QUORUM, with the other region copied asynchronously
caption: Two local acks make the write durable; the remote DC is updated in parallel but nobody waits for it.

messages.label: INSERT msg (LOCAL_QUORUM)
messages.note: The message id is a time-based UUID generated by the service, so a retry writes the same row instead of a duplicate.

messages.label: commit log + memtable
messages.note: B is one of the three local replicas, so its own write counts as the first ack.

messages.label: mutation
messages.note: Sent at the same time to one node in DC2, which forwards it to its local replicas. About 80 ms away.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: 2 of 3 local replicas: LOCAL_QUORUM is met.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: The third ack arrives later; it doesn't change the answer.

scenarios.name: Timeout, then retry
scenarios.summary: A timeout doesn't mean the write failed. Idempotent writes make retrying safe.

messages.label: write timeout
messages.note: A is in a GC pause and C is restarting: only B's own write landed within 2 s. The write may still land on A and C later.

messages.label: retry, same id 7f3…
messages.note: Same partition, same clustering key: it overwrites the same row, so there's no duplicate message.

scenarios.name: Link to DC2 down
scenarios.summary: LOCAL_QUORUM keeps DC1 writing during a cross-region outage; DC2 is repaired afterwards.

messages.label: ok
messages.note: Two local acks: the sender sees no difference.

messages.label: store hint for DC2
messages.note: Hints cover a short outage; after a long one, run repair so DC2 gets every missed message.

scenarios.name: Alternative: EACH_QUORUM
scenarios.summary: Waiting for a quorum in every DC gives cross-region read-your-writes, but each write pays a round trip to the other region, and a link failure stops writes.

messages.label: 2 DC2 acks (~80 ms)
messages.note: Two acks are needed from each DC.
